 Korea 4D3N Seoul Itinerary For K-Pop & K-Drama Fans, Including Filming Locations & Iconic Attractions
 4D3N Seoul i tinerary 
 Planning your next getaway to Seoul ? South Korea’s capital is packed with things to see and do, from centuries-old palaces and bustling shopping streets to trendy cafes and scenic parks. Plus, K-pop fans can visit filming locations featured in music videos by BTS, TWICE, and PSY.
 For those visiting South Korea’s capital for the 1st time, this 4D3N Seoul itinerary covers popular attractions, cultural experiences, shopping districts, and even a few K-drama filming spots. We’ve also included flight options from Singapore, hotel recommendations, estimated prices, and useful travel apps to help you plan your trip.
 The current exchange rate is S$1 = ~₩1037.30 as of 15th November 2026.

 How to get to Seoul from Singapore? 
 Image credit: Trip.com  
 Travellers can fly directly from Singapore Changi Airport to Incheon International Airport , with flights taking approximately 6 hours and 20 minutes .
 Several airlines operate direct affordable flights from Singapore to Seoul , including full-service and budget carriers.
 Here’s a breakdown of the airfares to expect:

 Do note that airfares are indicative and may vary depending on travel dates, availability, and booking conditions.
 Day 1 
 9.50am – Incheon Airport 
 Image credit: Incheon Airport 
 For this itinerary, we’re assuming a red-eye flight departing Singapore at 2.30am , with arrival at Incheon International Airport at 9.50am on the same day. Do factor in some time to clear immigration, collect your luggage, and travel to your accommodation in Myeongdong , where you can drop off your bags before heading out to explore the city.
 1 pm – Myeongdong Kyoja 
 Michelin Bib Gourmand eatery that has been around since 1966 
 Image credit: 명동교자 본점 via Google Maps 
 Kick off your Seoul adventure with a hearty lunch at Myeongdong Kyoja , a family-run restaurant that’s been serving traditional Korean dishes since 1966. With just 4 dishes on the menu, the restaurant keeps things simple, focusing on its well-loved noodle and dumpling recipes.
 Try the Kalguksu (₩8,000/~S$7.60) , a comforting bowl of hand-cut noodles served in a rich broth. Another crowd favourite is the Mandu (₩10,000/~S$9.60) , featuring generously filled Korean dumplings that pair well with the restaurant’s signature garlicky kimchi.
 Image credit: Tripadvisor 
 If you’re visiting during summer, you can also try the seasonal Kongguksu , a refreshing Korean summer dish featuring chilled noodles served in a creamy, nutty soybean broth, for ₩13,000 (~S$12.40) .
 Getting there: Take Subway Line 4 to Myeongdong Station , Exit 8 .

 K-pop merch for all the fans 
 Image adapted from: A A & Yj Oh via Google Maps 
 K-pop fans, prepare to put your shopping budget to work. Head to Myeongdong Underground Shopping Centre , located beneath Myeongdong Station, where you’ll find shops selling idol photocards, lightstick accessories, posters, and even K-pop-themed socks.  It’s a good stop for fans hoping to bring home merchandise from their favourite groups.
 For official merchandise, make your way to WITHMUU Myeongdong , where you can browse albums (from ₩15,000 / ~S$14.40) , official lightsticks (from ₩45,000 / ~S$43.30) , and other K-pop collectibles like photocard holders and accessories (from ₩3,000 / ~S$2.90) .
 Admission: Free to browse
 Location: Myeongdong Station (Line 4) and Myeongdong-gil, Seoul, South Korea

 Panoramic city views from a cable car 
 Image credit: Agoda 
 For a bird’s-eye view of the city, make your way to N Seoul Tower , perched atop Namsan Mountain . Take the Namsan Cable Car up the mountain and enjoy sweeping views of Seoul along the way. K-drama fans might recognise the cable car from the iconic date scene in Boys Over Flowers .
 Image credit: Netflix 
 For adults, a round-trip cable car ticket costs ₩15,000 (~S$14.40) , while a one-way ticket costs ₩12,000 (~S$11.50) . Children can enjoy a round trip for ₩11,500 (~S$11) or a one-way journey for ₩9,000 (~S$8.60) .
 Image credit: Klook 
 Alternatively, you can skip the cable car and hike up Mount Namsan to reach N Seoul Tower for free. There are several well-maintained walking paths and forest trails leading to the summit, including a popular 40-minute route from Baekbeom Square , near Myeongdong .
 Image adapted from: Seoul Korea via Facebook, Tripadvisor 
 The trail stretches approximately 1.9km , taking you past pine trees and sections of the historic Seoul City Wall , though do expect a steep climb with plenty of stairs.
 Another option is to start your hike from Dongguk University Station , where you can follow shaded walking paths and trails alongside the fortress walls towards the summit. Both routes offer a scenic alternative to the cable car, especially if you’d like to enjoy some fresh air and greenery along the way.
 Once you reach the tower, head up to its 360-degree observation deck for panoramic views of the city. Visiting around sunset is particularly scenic, as you can watch Seoul’s skyline gradually light up.
 Image credit: CHESTXRS_DOME via Reddit 
 Couples can also stop by the Love Lock Deck , where visitors attach personalised padlocks to the fences. If you’d rather spend some time outdoors, the surrounding Namsan Park has walking trails and scenic viewpoints. Padlocks can be bought, but feel free to bring your own.
 Here’s a breakdown of N Seoul Tower’s prices:
 Ticket Price 
 Observation Deck (13 years and above) ₩29,000 (~S$27.80) 
 Observation Deck (3-12 years and seniors aged 65+) ₩23,000 (~S$22) 
 Love Lock Deck Free 
 Padlocks ₩5,000 to ₩15,000 (~S$4.80 to S$14.30) 
 Getting there: Take Subway Line 4 to Myeongdong Station , Exit 1 , then walk uphill past Pacific Hotel towards the cable car station. Alternatively, take the free Namsan Oreumi inclined elevator , which generally operates from 9am-11pm , with scheduled maintenance on Mondays.

 Korean barbecue with premium beef & pork selections 
 Image credit: Tripadvisor 
 After an afternoon of sightseeing, satisfy your appetite at Wangbijib , a Korean barbecue restaurant in Myeongdong. Its name translates to “Imperial Princess’s House”, and the menu features a wide selection of grilled beef and pork dishes.
 Meat lovers can choose from cuts such as sirloin , tenderloin , beef belly , ox tongue , and marinated short ribs . Those dining in pairs can share the Assorted Pork Platter (₩33,000, ~S$31.60) , while beef lovers can opt for the Assorted Beef Platter (₩36,000, ~S$34.40) .
 Getting there: Take Subway Line 4 to Myeongdong Station , Exit 9 , followed by a 3 to 5-minute walk.

 Street food, Squid Game merchandise & late-night shopping 
 Image credit: Pat in Action via Google Maps 
 End your 1st day at Myeongdong Night Market , where the streets come alive with food stalls, souvenir shops, and shoppers. On busy evenings, the market is home to around 100 to 150 stalls .
 Myeongdong Night Market also makes an appearance in Netflix’s animated film KPop Demon Hunters , serving as the vibrant backdrop for the Saja Boys’ performance of their hit song Soda Pop .
 Image credit: Helena Baxter via Facebook 
 You’ll find stalls selling clothing , jewellery , accessories , and souvenirs . Keep an eye out for Squid Game -inspired merchandise, including tracksuits , figurines , and red guard plushies . Squid Game tracksuit tops cost approximately ₩35,000 (~S$33.50) , while player T-shirts are priced at around ₩20,000 (~S$19.10) .
 Good news; there’s plenty of food to munch on! For street food, t teokbokki costs around ₩5,000 (~S$4.80) , while d ragon’s b eard c andy is priced at ₩10,000 (~S$9.60) . You can also grab a Korean h ot d og for ₩2,500 (~S$2.40) , or g yeran-ppang , also known as egg bread, for ₩2,000 (~S$2) .
 Image adapted from: Williams Kyel, StephFaith Bautista & Alexander Wong via Google Maps 
 If you’re craving dumplings, k imchi m andu costs ₩7,000 (~S$6.70) , while b ulgogi m andu is priced at ₩8,000 (~S$7.60) . Other options include v egetable m andu for ₩6,000 (~S$5.70) and s oup m andu for ₩8,000 (~S$7.60) .
 Seafood lovers can try g rilled s quid for ₩12,000 (~S$11.50) , while d akgangjeong starts from ₩7,000 (~S$6.70) . Fans of Squid Game can also get their hands on d algona c andy for ₩5,000 (~S$4.80) .
 Getting there: Take Subway Line 4 to Myeongdong Station , Exits 6 , 7 , or 8 .

 9.45am – Gyeongbokgung Palace 
 Hanbok rentals at Seoul’s largest grand palace 
 Image credit: Circle Chow via Google Maps 
 Step back into the Joseon dynasty at Gyeongbokgung Palace , the largest of Seoul’s 5 grand palaces. Built in 1395, the palace once served as the main royal residence for the kings in the Joseon Dynasty, and is one of the city’s most iconic historical landmarks today.
 Image credit: Klook 
 For the full experience, rent a h anbok from one of the nearby rental shops and explore the palace grounds in traditional Korean attire. Visitors wearing qualifying hanbok can also enjoy free admission to the palaces.
 Don’t miss Geunjeongjeon Hall , where royal ceremonies and official meetings once took place. Another highlight is Gyeonghoeru Pavilion , a 2-storey structure overlooking a pond that was historically used for royal banquets.
 ARMYs, you might recognise this palace. BTS performed IDOL at the palace for The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon in 2020. In the same year, they also performed Mikrokosmos at the Gyeonghoeru Pavilion.
 Speaking of performances, you can also catch the Guard-on-Duty performance outside Gwanghwamun Gate at 11am and 1pm , with each performance lasting approximately 10 minutes . The performances are not held on Tuesdays.
 For hanbok rentals, a short rental of 1.5 to 2 hours typically costs from ₩5,000 (~S$4.80) . A half-day rental of 3 to 4 hours starts from ₩15,000 (~S$14.30) , while full-day rentals costs start from ₩18,000 (~S$17.20) .
 Book your hanbok rental here .
 Getting there: Take Subway Line 3 to Gyeongbokgung Station , Exit 5 , followed by a 3-minute walk.

 Contact Information +82 237003900 Google Reviews 4.6 (46,921) 12pm – Yeonghwaru 
 Korean-Chinese restaurant featured in the K-drama She Was Pretty 
 Image credit: cheon choi via Google Maps 
 Tucked away in the streets of Seochon , Yeonghwaru is a Korean-Chinese restaurant that has been serving hearty meals for over 50 years . Its nostalgic 1970s-style interiors, complete with walls covered in celebrity autographs, have also made it a filming location for the K-drama She Was Pretty . The restaurant appeared in a scene where Kim Jun-woo and Han Seol went on their 1st date over a meal of fiery dishes.
 Image adapted from: WSKIM, Kevin Ko & a k via Google Maps 
 One of its signature dishes is the Gochu Jajangmyeon (₩8,000/~S$7.60) , featuring black bean noodles topped with diced Cheongyang peppers, onions, and pork.
 Another popular option is the Gochu Jjamppong (₩8,000/~S$7.60) , a spicy seafood noodle soup with vegetables and a smoky, wok-fried flavour. For something less fiery, try the Tangsuyuk (₩25,000/~S$23.90) , featuring crispy battered pork served with sweet-and-sour sauce.
 You can also order Japchaebap (₩12,000/~S$11.60) , a rice dish topped with stir-fried glass noodles and vegetables. Fun fact: The restaurant serves its oolong tea in repurposed vintage Del Monte juice bottles , adding to its nostalgic atmosphere.
 Getting there: Take Subway Line 3 to Gyeongbokgung Station, Exit 2 , followed by a short walk into Seochon .

 Contact Information +82 027381218 Google Reviews 4 (870) 2pm – Bukchon Hanok Village 
 600-year-old hanok homes with IG-worthy backdrop of Seoul city 
 Image credit: Nguyễn Thành Hội via Google Maps 
 Continue your cultural adventure at Bukchon Hanok Village , a historic neighbourhood known for its beautifully preserved traditional Korean houses, or hanok. Located between Gyeongbokgung Palace, Changdeokgung Palace, and Jongmyo Shrine, the village offers a glimpse into Seoul’s architectural past.
 Image credit: PJ via Google Maps 
 Take a stroll along Bukchon-ro 11-gil , a picturesque street where traditional tiled rooftops are contrasted against Seoul’s modern skyline. You can also explore the Eight Scenic Views of Bukchon , a collection of viewpoints showcasing the neighbourhood’s architecture.
 Image adapted from: Trọng Ân, N P & Margot9485 via Google Maps 
 These views include Changdeokgung Palace , Wonseo-dong Handicraft Road , Gahoe-dong , Bukchon Observatory , the road uphill at Gahoe-dong , the stone stairway at Samcheong-dong , the house number 31 at Gahoe-dong , and the road downhill at Gahoe-dong.
 For something more hands-on, visit the Donglim Knot Museum , which displays traditional Korean decorative knots used in accessories, belts, and pouches. Selected workshops also let visitors try their hand at making their own knots.
 Image credit: YS K via Google Maps 
 Another attraction is The House of Baek Inje , a preserved hanok residence built in 1913 . Its architecture blends Korean design with early 20th-century influences, including Japanese-style corridors, tatami rooms, and red brickwork.
 Image credit: @backpackernat__ via Instagram 
 Fun fact: The K-drama Personal Taste , starring Lee Min-ho and Son Ye-jin, features Sanggojae , a traditional hanok house where the 2 main characters live together! While the house itself is a fictional residence, its traditional architecture reflects the charm of the hanok homes found throughout the village.
 Keep in mind that Bukchon Hanok Village is a residential neighbourhood. Noise levels should be kept down to respect the residents’ privacy while exploring. Visitors can only explore Bukchon Hanok Village between 10am and 5pm , as access is restricted outside these hours to minimise disturbances to residents.
 Getting there: Take Subway Line 3 to Anguk Station , Exit 2 , followed by a 10-minute walk.

 Korean souvenirs & handicraft boutiques 
 Image credit: Michael Mauer via Google Maps 
 If you’re looking for souvenirs beyond the usual fridge magnets, make your way to Insadong Culture Street . This cultural shopping district is lined with shops selling Korean pottery , handmade accessories , traditional stationery , and artwork .
 Image credit: あるふ via Google Maps 
 One spot worth visiting is Ssamziegil , a 4-storey shopping complex housing approximately 70 artisan boutiques and craft shops. Its spiral walkway connects all 4 floors, allowing visitors to browse the shops as they make their way upwards.
 You can also visit Jogyesa Temple , a Buddhist temple associated with the Jogye Order, or take a leisurely walk through Yeolrin Songhyeon Green Square . Depending on the season, the park features flowers such as cosmos, daisies, poppies, and peonies.
 Admission: Free to explore the shopping street
 Getting there: Take Subway Line 3 to Anguk Station , Exit 6 .

 Contact Information Google Reviews 4.3 (13,882) 5 . 30pm – HiKR Ground (Cheonggyecheon) 
 Playground with sets inspired by K-pop MVs 
 Image adapted from: Trip.com, Dave Chan via Google Maps 
 Ever wanted to star in your own K-pop music video? At HiKR Ground , an interactive tourism attraction operated by the Korea Tourism Organization, you can explore themed sets inspired by popular K-pop music videos.
 Head to K-Pop Ground on the 2nd floor , where you’ll find themed sets modelled after iconic music video scenes. These include the Laundromat Set, inspired by BTS’s Permission to Dance and Jennie’s SOLO , the Subway Train Set from aespa’s Black Mamba , and the Spaceship Set inspired by aespa’s Next Level .
 You can even customise the lighting, music, and visual backgrounds at these sets to recreate your favourite music video moments, film dance covers, or shoot your own TikTok videos.
 Admission: Free
 Getting there: Take Subway Line 1 to Jonggak Station , Exit 5 , followed by a 2-minute walk. Alternatively, take Subway Line 2 to Euljiro 1-ga Station , Exit 2 .

 Korean BBQ at Sun-jae’s father’s restaurant from K-drama Lovely Runner 
 Image credit: NK Ryu via Google Maps 
 Fans of Lovely Runner can relive moments from the K-drama at Soegojip , a traditional Korean BBQ restaurant in Insadong . The restaurant was featured in the series as the BBQ establishment owned by Ryu Sun-jae’s father, making it a familiar sight for viewers of the popular romance drama.
 Housed in a converted hanok , the restaurant features wooden beams, warm earthy tones, and a spacious interior that retains its traditional Korean architecture. Here, you can grill premium Hanwoo beef right at your table, with tender cuts of meat that pair perfectly with the restaurant’s selection of Korean side dishes.
 Image adapted from: Sophia Ha & Kevin Ko via Google Maps 
 Speaking of side dishes, diners can enjoy refillable banchan , including kimchi, pickled vegetables, fresh greens, and soup. These accompaniments balance out the richness of the grilled meat, making for a satisfying Korean BBQ experience.
 Expect to spend approximately ₩22,000 to ₩30,000 (~S$21 to S$28.70) per person , depending on your order.
 Getting there: Take Subway Lines 1, 3, or 5 to Jongno 3(sam)-ga Station, Exit 5 , followed by a short walk towards Insadong .

 Contact Information +82 01040404940 Google Reviews 4.4 (526) 8.15pm – Cheonggyecheon Stream walk 
 Outdoor library & night illuminations in the city centre 
 Image credit: Travel Stained via Facebook 
 If you’re visiting Seoul during the year-end festive season, add Cheonggyecheon Stream to your evening plans.
 The annual Seoul Lantern Festival , which takes place from 11th December 2026 to 31st January 2027 this year, is set to transform the waterway into a colourful display of illuminated sculptures and lantern installations.
 The festival began in 2009, and its 18th edition in 2026 will feature the theme “Romance of Seoul: Symphony of Light”. Visitors can enjoy large-scale light displays, themed installations, and interactive activities along the stream.
 Image credit: Tripadvisor 
 Besides the Seoul Lantern Festival , Cheonggyecheon Stream also hosts other seasonal celebrations throughout the year. In spring, the Lotus Lantern Festival , typically held between late April and mid-May to celebrate Buddha’s Birthday, illuminates the surrounding area with colourful traditional paper lanterns.
 Image adapted from: Agoda, Seoul Metropolitan Government 
 During summer, visitors can also look forward to Cheonggyecheon Water Splash , typically held between late July and early August . The event features a 120m-long splash zone stretching from Cheonggyecheon Waterfall to Gwangtonggyo Bridge , complete with free aqua-shoe rentals and waterside seating for visitors looking to cool off from the heat.
 Aside from its festivals, the stream is also a popular K-drama filming location, with its scenic walkways and waterfront setting appearing in hit series such as True Beauty , Queen of Tears , Lovely Runner , Marry My Husband , Vincenzo , and Lovestruck in the City .
 Admission: Free
 Getting there: Take Subway Line 5 to Gwanghwamun Station , Exit 5 .

 10 . 30am – Starfield Library & Ktown4u (Starfield COEX Mall) 
 Viral library & K-pop merch inside COEX Mall 
 Starfield Library. 
 Image credit: Diaries of A Travel Foodie via Google Maps  
 Start your 3rd day at Starfield Library , located inside Starfield COEX Mall in Gangnam. This viral photospot needs little introduction – you’ll most definitely have seen this on social media channels, as well as its newer cousin, Starfield Library Suwon.
 Beyond its towering bookshelves, Starfield Library has also made its way onto the small screen, appearing in popular K-dramas such as Record of Youth , Lovestruck in the City , and Personal Taste .
 Image credit: Helenaa via Google Maps 
 After exploring the library, head to Ktown4u COEX , located on the 2nd to 4th floors of COEX Artium . Here, K-pop fans can browse official albums , lightsticks , photocards , and other merchandise from their favourite artists.
 Depending on ongoing promotions, you may also find Lucky Draw photocard events . There’s even an Unboxing Zone , where fans can open their newly purchased albums and trade photocards.

 Just opposite COEX Mall is Bongeunsa Temple , a historic Buddhist temple that offers a peaceful escape from Gangnam’s busy streets. Originally established in 794 during the Silla dynasty, it was previously known as Gyeonseongsa Temple.
 The temple was renamed Bongeunsa in 1498, following renovations commissioned by Queen Jeonghyeon. Today, visitors can explore its traditional buildings, courtyards, and tranquil surroundings.
 Image credit: Nicolas Joaquin Rojas via Google Maps 
 Bongeunsa also houses 3,479 Buddhist scriptures across 13 categories. Traditional Buddhist ceremonies are still held here, including Jeongdaebulsa , which involves monks carrying scriptures and reciting Buddhist teachings.
 K-drama fans, you might recognise this place. The 1st episode of Faith: The Great Doctor features Bongeunsa Temple in a pivotal scene, where a mysterious time-travel portal opens and sets the stage for the drama’s journey between modern-day Korea and the Goryeo dynasty.
 Admission: Free

 Image credit: Trip.com  
 After all that shopping, spend some time outdoors at Seoul Forest , a sprawling public park in Seongsu-dong. The park features landscaped gardens, woodland paths, wetlands, and open spaces that are perfect for a relaxing afternoon.
 Seoul Forest has also served as a filming location for several popular K-dramas, including It’s Okay to Not Be Okay , Love Alarm , and The King: Eternal Monarch , with its picturesque greenery providing the backdrop for memorable scenes. Indulge yourself in a long photo-taking session to recreate these iconic K-drama moments.
 Image adapted from: Man Van Vinh & jeongtae lee via Google Maps 
 One of its highlights is the Eco Forest , where visitors can spot sika deer from an elevated walkway. Do keep in mind that feeding the sika deer is strictly prohibited for the health and safety of the deer.
 Other attractions include the Insect Garden , Butterfly Garden , and Wetland Ecological Park . For a leisurely afternoon, pack some snacks and enjoy a picnic at Green Square or near the duck pond. You can also rent a bicycle or pedal kart near Gate 5 to explore the park’s cycling paths.
 If you’re up for more walking, follow the pedestrian footbridge towards the Han River for views of the surrounding waterways.

 1. Naver Map 
 Navigating Seoul’s public transport system 
 Screenshot from: Naver Map 
 Getting around an unfamiliar city can be tricky, so download Naver Map ( App Store | Google Play ) before your trip. The navigation app provides detailed directions, public transport routes, real-time traffic updates, and walking instructions.
 It’s particularly useful for identifying subway exits and planning journeys between attractions. You can also save places to personalised lists and check business opening hours, including restaurant break times.
 2. Papago 
 Translating Korean menus, signs & conversations 
 Image credit: Google Play 
 If you don’t speak Korean, Papago ( App Store | Google Play ) is a handy translation app to have on your phone. Developed by Naver, it supports Korean, English, and several other languages.
 Its Image Translation feature allows you to photograph Korean menus, signs, and written instructions for translation. You can also use the app to communicate with locals when language barriers arise.
 3. k.ride 
 Booking taxis with international payment cards 
 Image credit: k.ride  
 For times when public transport isn’t the most convenient option, k.ride ( App Store | Google Play ) lets international visitors book taxis in South Korea. The app has an English-language interface and supports eligible international credit cards. It’s particularly useful when travelling with luggage or heading back to your hotel after public transport services have ended.
 4. Baemin 
 Food delivery app 
 Image credit: SmartOSC 
 Craving Korean fried chicken after a long day of sightseeing? Baemin ( App Store | Google Play ), also known as Baedal Minjok, is a popular food delivery app that lets users order from nearby restaurants.
 You can browse dishes such as jjajangmyeon, tteokbokki, and Korean fried chicken, then have them delivered to your accommodation. The app is primarily in Korean, so Papago may be helpful when navigating its menus.
 Make the most of your trip with this 4D3N Seoul itinerary 
 There’s plenty more to Seoul than its famous tourist attractions. This itinerary covers a mix of cultural landmarks, popular shopping districts, and food spots to help you experience different sides of the city.
 Of course, there’s no need to follow every stop down to the minute. Leave some room to wander through smaller streets, discover independent cafés, and explore places that catch your eye. After all, some of the best travel memories happen when you venture beyond your planned itinerary.
